research_question: does a score still discriminate between patients the confounder cannot separate
estimator: c_W = P(score_malignant > score_benign | |C_mal - C_ben| <= W), ties 0.5; caliper 'none' recovers the ordinary AUROC exactly
stratum_rationale: a caliper bounds the distance on a continuous confounder; it does not hold an acquisition session constant, and a label-pure session is a shortcut the caliper leaves open
control_orientation: fixed once on the full cohort (sign = +1)
control_rationale: the confounder's own c_W must fall towards 0.5 as the caliper narrows; that it does is what shows the caliper controls it
decision_rule: improvement demonstrated only when delta_ci_lower > 0; an interval containing zero means not demonstrated, not equivalent
bootstrap: patients resampled within class, admissible pairs recomputed per draw
caveat: the caliper controls what the *evaluation* pairs can differ by; it does not remove a shortcut a model trained on the full cohort may already have learned. Training on a matched cohort is the complementary experiment.
